verdict: Take-Two's revenue rose 2% to $1.5B on steady in-game spending, but a $43M write-off on a cancelled game and heavy acquisition amortization left it with a $34M net loss ahead of the GTA VI launch.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: net revenue $1.53B vs $1.50B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted net loss per share, vs -$0.07 a year ago

kpis.label: Net Bookings
kpis.note: down 3% YoY — games sold, before deferrals

segments.name: Game revenue
segments.note: Game sales and in-game spending — NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption and Zynga mobile games — up 3%. Recurrent consumer spending (virtual currency, add-ons and in-game purchases) was $1,290M of this, 84% of total revenue.

segments.name: Advertising revenue
segments.note: In-game advertising, mostly in mobile games — down 8%.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Marketing games and buying players for mobile titles — the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building games at Rockstar, 2K and Zynga studios.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of equipment and other assets over their lives (acquired-game amortization sits in cost of revenue).

takeaways.title: Players keep spending in old games
takeaways.text: Recurrent consumer spending — virtual currency, add-on content and in-game purchases — was $1,290M, 84% of revenue, led by NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto Online and Zynga mobile titles such as Toon Blast and Empires & Puzzles.

takeaways.title: A GAAP loss, by design of the calendar
takeaways.text: The $34M net loss includes $161M of non-cash amortization of intangibles from past acquisitions and a $43M impairment on a cancelled title. The big release — Grand Theft Auto VI, due November 19, 2026 — lands in the next quarter but one.

takeaways.title: Bookings dipped slightly
takeaways.text: Net Bookings — what was actually sold in the quarter, before revenue deferrals — fell 3% to $1,386M. Mobile was half of revenue at $762M, console $641M and PC and other $131M.

oneTimers: Cost of revenue included a $43.4M impairment charge after Take-Two decided not to proceed with an unannounced title from a third-party developer — the main reason software development costs and royalties jumped to $135M from $30M a year ago.
otherDetail: Interest and other, net was a $14M expense: $23M of interest income, less $30M of interest expense and $6M of other expense, net (rounded). A $15M tax benefit then reduced the $49M pre-tax loss to a $34M net loss.
footerNote: Take-Two had not yet reported fiscal Q2 2027 (ended September 30, 2026) as of November 7, 2026, so this page covers its latest reported quarter, fiscal Q1 2027. Amounts are rounded to the nearest $M from the release's $0.1M figures; operating loss is shown as $35M (reported $35.5M). The chart draws the $34M net loss as covered by cash on hand — the shortfall came from the balance sheet, not from revenue.
